      Model notes

      • Joists are an assumed layout: 16″ o.c. from the first joist ≈4¼″ off the west wall. New ducts sit at bay centres, within 4″ of the positions on M-1.
      • S-1 and S-5 are top takeoffs. The soffit faces are ≈3″ off the trunk, too tight for a side takeoff and elbow.
      • Approximate: existing return height, furnace and water-heater size, the upstairs ducts past the trunk, the fresh-air flex route, window sill heights, foundation thickness.
      • Furniture: the office pieces are a suggested layout for the desk, bookshelf and 3D printer. The play area and storage shelving are examples only; you haven’t planned furniture there.
      • Not modelled: door casing, window returns, cable runs, water lines, furnace vent pipes, blocking for the barn-door track.

      Basement Build Book

      48 sheets and 25 steps, from the permit to the final inspection. One drawing per assembly, each with its own bill of materials.

      How to use this book

      1. Each assembly has its own sheet: a drawing, numbered bubbles on the parts, and a bill of materials that uses the same numbers.
      2. Bubble numbers are fixed on the wall sheets (1 = PT bottom plate … 16 = tie plate, see G-2); on the other sheets they count from 1 per sheet.
      3. The Buy column points at the line in the BOM & Budget workbook (B-###), so every part traces back to a price and a buy lot.
      4. Dimensions are from the bare concrete: x from the west foundation wall, y from the north foundation wall, heights above the slab.
      5. The joist layout is assumed (16″ o.c., first joist centre 5″ off the west wall). Check it in step 3 and adjust blocking, duct bays and grid lines to the real joists.
      6. The step instructions say which sheet and bubble to use. Each sheet’s title block lists the steps that use it.

      How the build runs

      One permit, one all-trades rough inspection, a separate insulation inspection, then the final. Nothing gets covered before its inspection.

      Phase 1 (through March): all rough-in, all drywall hung, and every finish in the office, bath, mech, storage and utility, about 290 hours. Phase 2: open-area finishes, about 83 hours.

      Each step below names the sheets it uses. Bubbles like 4 match the numbers on that sheet’s drawing and its bill of materials.

      Hold points

      • Step 1 · Permit posted before any work.
      • Step 5 · Optional look by Mike before framing.
      • Step 9 · DWV test holding for the rough inspection.
      • Step 12 · Mike signs off before insulation.
      • Step 14 · Mike signs off before drywall.
      • Step 25 · Final inspection.

      Permit

      Phase 1 · ≈4 h · buy lot —

      No drawing

      Do this

      1. Fill in both forms: living area ≈784 sq ft, unfinished ≈357 sq ft, owner as the builder for all trades.
      2. Email the permit set and forms to Mike Leifker (mleifker@villageofbellevuewi.gov, 920-593-5504) or drop them at 3100 Eaton Rd. Point out that the sink vent ties into the existing 2″ riser (no AAV).
      3. Ask Mike two things now: whether he wants to see the box-sill foam before framing hides it, and whether he wants a look at the end of Phase 1.
      4. Post the permit card where it can be seen from the stair.

      Before you start

      • The Sep 30 permit set (PDF) and the forms BI-204-A and BI-204-B.

      Check before moving on

      • Permit card posted. Nothing, including foam, goes on a wall before this.
      Hold point Permit posted before any work.

      Buy Lot 1

      Phase 1 · ≈3 h · buy lot 1

      No drawing

      Do this

      1. Menards: foam, box-sill foam, framing lumber, fasteners, cable, boxes, duct parts, plumbing rough parts.
      2. Home Depot: breakers, alarms, bath fan, grilles, 4″ wall cap (B-052 to B-056, B-073, B-078, B-082, B-083, B-107, B-109).
      3. Store the foam flat and the lumber on stickers off the slab; keep PT lumber out of the sun.
      4. Check the breaker part numbers against the panel label (Siemens type QP) before leaving the store.

      3

      Prepare, flow-test the drains and snap the layout

      Phase 1 · ≈10 h · buy lot 1

      G-1Key plan and assembly tagsL-1Layout plan · north halfL-2Layout plan · south half

      Do this

      1. Clear and vacuum the slab along every wall line.
      2. Uncap the 4″ toilet stub and the 2″ sink stub. Run a garden hose into each for 5 minutes. Both must drain freely. If either backs up, or water shows anywhere else, stop and call before going further: the bath design assumes they join under the slab.
      3. Mark the exact centre of the 4″ drain on the slab. Recap both stubs with tape and a test plug so nothing falls in.
      4. Set out the bath east wall first from that centre: plate west edge 12¾″ east of the drain centre, so the drywall lands at 12¼″ L-2.
      5. Snap every plate line from the tables on L-1 and L-2: each row names the plate edge the line marks and its distance from the concrete. Furring-wall plates sit 1″ off the concrete because the XPS goes behind them.
      6. Mark door and opening edges in red on the slab: bath 272″–306″, storage 358″–396″, barn opening 85¾″–132¾″, utility 14″–46″, mech bifold 231″–293″ from the north wall.
      7. Check the office and the bath for square with a 3-4-5 triangle before snapping the long lines.
      8. Look up: write the real joist positions on the plan. The book assumes 16″ o.c. with the first joist centre 5″ off the west wall. If yours differ, move blocking, duct bays and the grid lines to suit.

      Before you start

      • Basement cleared to the slab; shop vac; chalk line, 25′ tape, 4′ level, laser or long straightedge.

      Check before moving on

      • Both drains flow. Every wall line on the slab matches the L sheets within ⅛″.
      4

      Foam the foundation walls

      Phase 1 · ≈14 h · buy lot 1

      EN-11″ XPS on the foundation walls

      Do this

      1. Cut the 1″ XPS 13 to 92½″ (slab to the top of the foundation) and stand sheets vertically, following the sheet layout on EN-1 wall by wall.
      2. Adhesive A in vertical beads 16″ apart. Press the sheet on, ¼″ off the slab; brace for 10 minutes where the wall is out of plane.
      3. Tape every vertical seam T.
      4. Low-expansion foam F along the bottom gap, the top edge at the sill plate and every inside corner.
      5. Cut neatly around the office and open-area windows; the drywall return covers the edge later (DW-2 D).
      6. No foam on the storage and utility walls, and keep clear of the sump pit.

      Before you start

      • Permit posted (step 1). Concrete dry and clean.

      Check before moving on

      • No gaps at seams, top or bottom. Foam stays exposed only until step 15: the drywall is its thermal barrier (SPS 321.11).
      5

      Seal the box sill

      Phase 1 · ≈12 h · buy lot 1

      EN-2Box sill: cut-and-seal foam

      Do this

      1. Work only the rim bays over the insulated walls: office, open area, half bath, mech south. Skip storage and utility.
      2. Pull the existing batt out of each bay Bt and vacuum the bay.
      3. Cut 2″ XPS R ⅛″ smaller than the bay (about 14½″ × 9¼″), press it to the rim, and foam all four edges F.
      4. Along the west wall the joists run parallel to the rim: foam the strip between the rim and the first joist in 4′ pieces.
      5. Push the batt back in against the foam and hold it with wire or staples (SPS 322.21(1)).

      Before you start

      • Wall foam done (step 4).

      Check before moving on

      • Every bay sealed on four edges and the batt back in place. If Mike wanted to see it, call now.
      Hold point Optional look by Mike before framing.
      6

      Frame the furring walls

      Phase 1 · ≈20 h · buy lot 1

      G-2Standard framing detailsFW-1Open-area west furring wallFW-2.1Open-area north furring wall · part 1 of 2FW-2.2Open-area north furring wall · part 2 of 2FW-3Open-area east furring wallFW-4Office west furring wallFW-5Office south furring wallFW-6Mech south furring wallFW-7Half-bath furring walls

      Do this

      1. Work one wall sheet at a time. Cut the plates from the sheet’s cut list: PT bottom plate 1 and SPF top plate 3, joints on stud centres.
      2. Lay the two plates side by side and mark every stud, king and jack from the sheet’s stud-centre row so top and bottom match.
      3. Sill gasket 2 on the slab line, PT plate on top, inner edge on the chalk line. Drill and drive Tapcons 14 about 24″ apart, within 6″ of each end, two per piece minimum.
      4. Top plate: where the wall crosses the joists (FW-2, FW-5, FW-6, FW-7) nail it up into every joist 15. Where it runs parallel to the joists (FW-1, FW-3, FW-4) install the 2x4 blocking 12 between joists first, at the spacing shown, and nail the plate to it.
      5. Plumb the top plate over the bottom plate with a level or laser at each end, then every 4′.
      6. Measure each stud 4 between the plates (the slab and the joists are not flat) and cut it to fit snug, about 90⅝″. End-nail or toe-nail per G-2.
      7. Windows on FW-1 and FW-4: kings 5, jacks 6, flat header 7, rough sill 9 and cripples 8, 10 as drawn, opening edges at the sheet’s dimensions.
      8. Tie-plate 16 every top-plate splice and corner.

      Before you start

      • Foam (step 4) and box sill (step 5) done. Hammer drill, 3/16″ masonry bit, framing nailer with 3¼″ HDG nails.

      Check before moving on

      • Every wall straight to a string within ¼″ and plumb. Stud centres match the sheet so the drywall and batts fit.
      7

      Frame the partitions and openings

      Phase 1 · ≈26 h · buy lot 1

      G-2Standard framing detailsPW-1Utility closet east wallPW-2Utility closet south wallPW-3.1Beam-line wall · part 1 of 2PW-3.2Beam-line wall · part 2 of 2PW-4Office east wallPW-5Bath west wallPW-6Bath alcove wall, north–southPW-7Bath alcove wall, east–westPW-8Bath east wallHV-5Combustion air and duct sealingDR-2Prehung doors and bifold

      Do this

      1. Beam-line wall PW-3.1 PW-3.2: PT plate on gasket along the line, top plate snug under the beam and nailed up into it. Studs are about 81¾″. Both plates stop ¼″ short of each steel post (3½″ gap), with a stud on each side of the post; never cut, notch or drill a post. Glue down the short PT blocks between a post and a door opening.
      2. Openings in the beam-line wall: no header fits under the top plate, and none is needed in this non-bearing wall, so the top plate is the head. Barn opening 47″ × 83¼″ (to the top plate). Bath door 34″ × 82½″ and storage door 38″ × 82½″: jacks 6 at 82½″ with a 1x4 laid flat 17 on them, nailed up into the top plate.
      3. Combustion-air openings in the same wall, between studs: high 14″ × 14″ at 182″–196″ with its top at the top plate; low 14″ × 14″ at 230″–244″, 3″ off the floor. Flat 2x4 blocking 11 under the high one and above and below the low one (HV-5).
      4. Office east wall PW-4: under the trunk it stops at 84¾″; the full-height part starts at the soffit edge (225⅜″). Bifold rough opening 62″ × 82″ at 231″–293″.
      5. Bath walls PW-5 to PW-8 the same way: the parts under the trunk stop at 84¾″. PW-8 is set from the drain centre (step 3).
      6. Utility closet PW-1 PW-2: door rough opening 32″ × 82½″ at 14″–46″ from the north wall, swinging out.
      7. Where a partition meets a furring wall, add the flat stud backing shown on G-2 (detail 4) so both drywall faces have something to land on.
      8. Leave the bottom plate in every door opening for now; cut it out just before the doors go in (step 20).

      Before you start

      • Furring walls up (step 6).

      Check before moving on

      • Every rough opening matches DR-2 (door width + 2″, 82½″ high). Bath east wall finished face will be 12¼″ from the drain centre.
      8

      Rough-in the ductwork and the bath fan

      Phase 1 · ≈14 h · buy lot 1

      HV-1Supply branches S-1 and S-5HV-2Supply branches S-2, S-3, S-4HV-3Return grille R-1HV-4Half-bath exhaust fanHV-5Combustion air and duct sealing

      Do this

      1. S-1 and S-5 HV-1: cut the collar holes in the TOP of the trunk ¾″ in from its south edge, at x = 45″ (6″) and x = 285″ (4″). Fit the start collars 1, elbow 2 up into the bay, pipe 3 south, damper 4 just past the soffit face, boot 5 hung with its bottom at 90″.
      2. At S-5 leave about 6″ of the trunk top clear for the existing upstairs duct that leaves the same bay northward.
      3. S-2, S-3, S-4 HV-2: collars 1 on the trunk’s north face at 77″, 253″ and 381″, two 45s 2 up into the bay, pipe north over the beam, damper 4 at 169″, boot centred 101″ from the north wall. S-2’s boot jogs 4″ east to 81″ so it lands inside a tile.
      4. R-1 HV-3: cut a 10″ × 20″ opening in the panned return at 77″ from the north wall, bend the sleeve 2 down to 90″ and seal it to the pan with mastic 4.
      5. Mastic every seam of the return inside the mech room (HV-5 5).
      6. Bath fan HV-4: housing 1 between the joists at 317″, 4¼″ hole 5 through the south rim over the patio slab, 4″ rigid duct 3 sloped toward the cap, wall cap 4 sealed to the rim.
      7. Fresh-air flex: look for a backdraft flap at the outside hood or the collar. None? Fit the damper 4 on HV-5 now, before the office soffit closes over it.
      8. Tape every joint with UL 181 foil tape, strap every 4′ and at each boot.

      Before you start

      • Furnace off at the switch while cutting into the trunk.

      Check before moving on

      • All five registers, R-1 and the fan grille land inside a tile on the CL-1 grid. Every damper is reachable from below.
      9

      Rough-in the plumbing

      Phase 1 · ≈10 h · buy lot 1

      PL-1Sink drain and ventPL-2Water supply to the half bath

      Do this

      1. Drain PL-1 A: glue a 2″ stub-up 1 into the slab stub, two 45s 2 to bring it into the bath west wall cavity, and a sanitary tee 3 with the trap adapter facing the room at 19″.
      2. Vent: 2″ pipe 4 up the cavity, through a 2⅝″ hole 7 in the top plate, elbow 5 north in the joist bay at x ≈ 265″ for about 6½′ to y = 231″, elbow west.
      3. Bore one 2⅝″ hole 8 through the joist at 261″, centred in its depth and ≥2″ from both edges PL-1 C.
      4. Strap the existing 2″ riser above and below, cut out a section at 98⅝″, and fit the new sanitary tee 6 with two no-hub couplings 11.
      5. Water PL-2: tee 1 2 into the hot and cold over the water heater, run ½″ PEX 3 south in that bay and east through ¾″ holes 6 to the vanity wall; cold continues east to the bath east wall.
      6. Stub-outs on flat 2x4 blocks 7: vanity hot and cold at 21″, 4″ apart, hot on the left; toilet 8″ high, 6″ north of the drain centre 5.
      7. Test: plug the trap adapter 9 and the 4″ stub 10, fill the vent with water to the top and leave it. Cap the PEX and leave it under house pressure.

      Before you start

      • Bath walls framed (step 7). Water off and drained before cutting the supply lines.

      Check before moving on

      • No drop in the vent water level after 15 minutes; no drips on the PEX.
      Hold point DWV test holding for the rough inspection.
      10

      Rough-in the electrical

      Phase 1 · ≈30 h · buy lot 1

      EL-1Panel and circuit scheduleEL-2Office circuits A and BEL-3Open-area receptacles, circuit CEL-4Open-area lights, circuit DEL-5Half-bath circuit EEL-6Mech, storage, utility and alarms

      Do this

      1. Panel EL-1: new breakers A (19), B (21), C (23), D (25), E (27). Swap 9, 15 and the alarm circuit to AFCI / dual-function, same rating; confirm each has its own neutral first.
      2. Boxes: single-gang new-work boxes, set ½″ proud of the stud face so they finish flush with the drywall. Receptacles 16″, switches 48″, bath GFCI 42″ to the box centre (EL-1 mounting heights).
      3. Set every box from the device tables on EL-2, EL-3, EL-5 and EL-6. Nothing on the open-area face of the beam wall between 38″ and 134″ (barn door).
      4. Office EL-2: A to the east-wall receptacle and along the south wall. B to the switch box first, switch leg to the 4 wafer spots, then on to the GFCI at the north wall 2 and from its LOAD to the other three receptacles.
      5. Open area EL-3 EL-4: C around the 12 receptacles. D: new 3-way at the office opening, 12/3 to the stair bottom where the 4-way goes in, 12/2 to the 12 wafer spots. Leave a 2′ loop at each wafer spot above the grid line.
      6. Phase 1 light: put keyless lampholders on 3 of the D wafer feeds at joist level.
      7. Bath EL-5: E home run to the GFCI receptacle 1, LOAD to the 2-gang switch box 2, then to the 2 wafers and the fan.
      8. Mech, storage, utility EL-6: extend 9 to the keyless lights and switches, 15 to the two receptacles. Move the smoke/CO to the stair bottom on blocking at joist level, interconnected.
      9. Staple within 12″ of each box and every 4½′; nail plates wherever cable is within 1¼″ of a stud face. Make up grounds in every box; leave 6″ of free conductor.

      Before you start

      • Your electrical resource has confirmed the breakers and where circuit D lands at the existing stair switches (EL-4 note 1). Main breaker off for panel work.

      Check before moving on

      • Every box at the right height and depth. Breakers labelled. Nothing energised that isn’t terminated.
      11

      Frame the soffits

      Phase 1 · ≈8 h · buy lot 1

      SF-1Office soffitSF-2Bath soffit and beam wrap

      Do this

      1. Ledger 1 screwed to the beam-line wall top plate along each soffit, underside at 83½″. Nothing fastens to the beam.
      2. Build each face ladder flat on the floor: rails 3 5 and uprights 4 at 16″. Lift it, line the face up with a string at 225⅜″ (office) or 224⅞″ (bath), screw the top rail into every joist.
      3. Rungs 2 every 24″ from the ledger to the bottom rail, underside level at 83½″.
      4. Close the soffit ends where they meet a wall cavity with 2x2 and drywall (fireblocking, SPS 321.085).

      Before you start

      • All ducts, pipes and cables above the soffits done and taped (steps 8–10).

      Check before moving on

      • Soffit bottom flat and level at 83½″; the face is a straight line; every damper beyond the face is still reachable.

      Insulate the walls

      Phase 1 · ≈10 h · buy lot 2

      IN-1Wall insulation

      Do this

      1. Only the furring walls get batts; partitions stay empty.
      2. Cut each R-13 kraft batt 1 to the bay height on a board with a straightedge.
      3. Press it in to touch the XPS, kraft face to the room, and staple the flanges 2 to the FACE of each stud about every 8″.
      4. Split batts around cables 8; cut them around boxes 7 and pipes, never stuff behind.
      5. Fireblock foam 9 every wire and pipe hole in a top plate.

      Before you start

      • Rough inspection signed (step 12). Lot 2 bought.

      Check before moving on

      • No gaps, folds or torn paper; R-13 labels readable.

      Insulation inspection

      Phase 1 · ≈1 h · buy lot —

      IN-1Wall insulation

      Do this

      1. Call Mike for the insulation inspection. Keep the batt bags with labels on site.

      Before you start

      • All batts in, labels visible.

      Check before moving on

      • Signed.
      Hold point Mike signs off before drywall.
      15

      Hang the drywall in every room

      Phase 1 · ≈40 h · buy lot 2

      DW-1Drywall: takeoff and board layoutDW-2Drywall details

      Do this

      1. Hang every room, the open area included, so no foam stays exposed while you live with the basement between phases (SPS 321.11).
      2. Foundation walls: top course first, tight to the joists, horizontal; bottom course ripped, ½″ off the slab 4, factory edge up (DW-1).
      3. Butt joints on studs 2, staggered; no joint lined up with a door or window edge.
      4. Screws 3 16″ o.c. on studs, ⅜″ from the edges; 12″ on soffit bottoms.
      5. Soffits: bottom first, then the face; corner bead on the bottom edge (DW-2 B).
      6. Beam wrap: ½″ drywall screwed to the beam from 85″ to the joists, bead on the bottom edge (DW-2 C).
      7. Window returns into the openings with bead on the room edge (DW-2 D).
      8. Partitions get both faces.

      Before you start

      • Insulation inspection signed (step 14). Box, pipe and cable locations marked on the floor.

      Check before moving on

      • Every foam surface covered, top to bottom. Every box and grille opening cut clean.
      16

      Tape, mud and sand

      Phase 1 (16a) · 2 (16b) · ≈20 + 25 h · buy lot 2

      DW-2Drywall details

      Do this

      1. 16a, Phase 1: office, bath, mech and both soffits. 16b, Phase 2: open area and the beam wrap.
      2. Tape coat: paper tape bedded in all-purpose compound on every flat joint and inside corner; first coat over the bead flanges.
      3. Fill coat, then a finish coat, each wider than the last; sand between with a sponge.
      4. Above 90″ one coat of tape is enough: it is hidden by the ceiling but must stay continuous over the foam.

      Before you start

      • Drywall hung (step 15).

      Check before moving on

      • Joints invisible under a work light held along the wall.
      17

      Prime and paint the walls

      Phase 1 (17a) · 2 (17b) · ≈9 + 11 h · buy lot 2

      FN-1Paint and trim

      Do this

      1. 17a: office, bath, mech. 17b: open area.
      2. One coat of PVA primer on all new drywall.
      3. Two coats of eggshell to 90″ (the ceiling line). Storage and utility can stay unpainted.

      Before you start

      • Mud dry and sanded. Before the grid and the floor, so nothing needs masking.

      Check before moving on

      • Even sheen, no flashing over the joints.
      18

      Hang the ceiling grid

      Phase 1 (18a) · 2 (18b) · ≈9 + 15 h · buy lot 3

      CL-1Ceiling grid, reflected plan

      Do this

      1. 18a: office and bath. 18b: open area.
      2. Laser a level line at 90″ around each room and screw the wall angle 1 to the studs through the drywall, along the soffit faces too.
      3. Mark the grid lines from CL-1 on the wall angle: they are set so every light, register, grille and the fan lands inside a tile.
      4. Screw eyes 6 into the joists and hang 12 ga wires 5 every 4′ along each main line, pulled tight.
      5. Main tees 2 east–west, levelled to the wall angle; 4′ cross tees 3 north–south every 2′; 2′ cross tees 4 between them.
      6. 18b only: replace the temporary keyless lights with the 12 wafers (EL-4) and drop the smoke/CO to a grid box hanger.

      Before you start

      • Walls painted (step 17). Lot 3 bought.

      Check before moving on

      • Grid level within ⅛″ over 10′; tees square; tiles wait until step 24.
      19

      Lay the LVP floor

      Phase 1 (19a) · 2 (19b) · ≈8 + 12 h · buy lot 3

      FL-1LVP flooring plan

      Do this

      1. 19a: office and bath. 19b: open area. Mech, storage and utility stay concrete.
      2. Undercut door jambs 5 with a jamb saw before laying near them.
      3. Planks 1 east–west in the office and open area; stagger end joints ≥8″; leave the expansion gap 2 at every wall and post.
      4. T-molding 3 in the bath doorway; reducer 4 at the storage door and the mech opening.

      Before you start

      • LVP acclimated 48 hours in the basement. The LVP install guide read (slab moisture, flatness, poly).

      Check before moving on

      • No hollow spots, gaps tight, expansion gap everywhere the base will cover.
      20

      Hang the doors

      Phase 1 · ≈12 h · buy lot 3

      DR-1Office barn doorDR-2Prehung doors and bifold

      Do this

      1. Cut the bottom plate 4 out of each door opening, flush with the jacks.
      2. Prehung doors 1 DR-2: set the hinge jamb plumb with shims 2 at each hinge, then the head and strike side, trim-head screws through the shims. Even ⅛″ gap around the slab.
      3. Bath door slab 1″ above the finished floor: it is the bath’s air path.
      4. Bifold pair in the mech opening, louvers facing the office.
      5. Barn door DR-1: lag the track 2 through the beam wrap into the beam, every hole, ≥2½″ into the wood 3; hangers and stops 4; door 1 1″ above the LVP, no sweep; floor guide 5 at the west edge of the opening.

      Before you start

      • Floor down (step 19a).

      Check before moving on

      • Doors swing and latch without binding; the barn door parks over 37¾″–85¾″ and closes over the opening.
      21

      Electrical trim-out

      Phase 1 (21a) · 2 (21b) · ≈7 + 5 h · buy lot 3

      EL-2Office circuits A and BEL-3Open-area receptacles, circuit CEL-4Open-area lights, circuit DEL-5Half-bath circuit EEL-6Mech, storage, utility and alarms

      Do this

      1. 21a: office, bath, mech, storage, utility. 21b: open area receptacles, switches and plates.
      2. Receptacles and switches; GFCIs at the office north wall (LINE from the switch box) and the bath (first on E).
      3. Wafers clipped into their tiles at trim-out (each has its own junction box), keyless fixtures on their boxes.
      4. Test every GFCI and AFCI with its test button and a plug-in tester; test the alarm interconnect from each alarm.

      Before you start

      • Paint done. Breakers off.

      Check before moving on

      • Every device works, every protective device trips and resets, every alarm sounds all four.
      22

      Plumbing trim

      Phase 1 · ≈8 h · buy lot 3

      PL-3Toilet and vanity

      Do this

      1. Closet flange 1 glued inside the 4″ stub, sitting on the finished floor.
      2. Toilet 3 on the wax-free seal and bolts 2: 12¼″ from the drain centre to the finished east wall.
      3. Vanity 4 centred on the drain, faucet 5, P-trap 8 into the trap adapter, stops and supplies 6.
      4. Water on; check every joint, then check again after 24 hours.

      Before you start

      • LVP down in the bath (step 19a).

      Check before moving on

      • No drips, toilet solid, trap holds water.
      23

      Base, casing, caulk and trim paint

      Phase 1 (23a) · 2 (23b) · ≈9 + 7 h · buy lot 3

      FN-1Paint and trim

      Do this

      1. 23a: office, bath, doors. 23b: open area.
      2. Base 1 on the LVP, nailed into studs and the bottom plate, not the floor; coped inside corners, mitred outside.
      3. Casing 2 with a ¼″ reveal on the jamb, mitred heads, 2″ brads 3 every 16″.
      4. Fill and caulk 4, then two coats of semi-gloss 5.

      Before you start

      • Floors and doors in.

      Check before moving on

      • Tight joints, no nail holes showing.
      24

      Drop in the ceiling tiles

      Phase 1 (24a) · 2 (24b) · ≈3 + 5 h · buy lot 3

      CL-1Ceiling grid, reflected plan

      Do this

      1. 24a: office and bath. 24b: open area.
      2. Cut border tiles face up with a sharp knife; tiles 7 with registers, wafers and the fan cut to the fixture.
      3. Leave the tiles under each damper ((8), dashed L on CL-1) unclipped so they lift out.

      Before you start

      • Everything above the grid finished and tested.

      Check before moving on

      • Every damper reachable through a lift-out tile.
      25

      Safety checks and final inspection

      Phase 1 (25a) · 2 (25b) · ≈2 + 3 h · buy lot —

      HV-5Combustion air and duct sealing

      Do this

      1. 25a, end of Phase 1: spillage test at the water heater draft hood with the range hood, every bath fan and the dryer on high and the furnace blower running. Smoke or a lighter flame must pull into the hood within a minute.
      2. Set the dampers so each room gets at least 1 air change per hour; mark the damper handles.
      3. Test alarms, GFCIs and AFCIs again. Ask Mike if he wants a look now.
      4. 25b, end of Phase 2: repeat the spillage test with the same lineup, rebalance the dampers, post the insulation certificate at the panel, call for the final.

      Before you start

      • Mech room enclosed, bath fan running.

      Check before moving on

      • Water heater drafts under the worst case; final signed.
      Hold point Final inspection.

      4. Hang wires before the mains: ≤4′ apart along each main, pulled tight, three turns. Level the mains to the wall angle.
      5. Phase 1: office and bath grid (step 18a), tiles last (step 24a). Phase 2: open area (18b), then swap the keyless lights for the wafers.
